raw_segments.text: Little Tumai attended to Kala Nag's supper, and as evening fell, wandered through the
camp, unspeakably happy, in search of a tom-tom.
When an Indian child's heart is full, he does not run about and make a noise in an
He sits down to a sort of revel all by himself, and Little Tumai had been spoken to by Peterson
If he had not found what he wanted, I believe he would have been ill.
But the sweet-meat cellar in the camp lent him a little tom-tomma drum beaten with the
hand-end he sat down, cross-legged, before Kala Nag as the stars began to come out, the
tom-tom in his lap, and he thumped and he thumped and he thumped, and the more he thought
of the great honour that had been done to him, the more he thumped, all alone among
There was no tune and no words, but the thumping made him happy.
